summary: One-shot RFB handshake reads the version banner and the security-type list. Detects security-type 1 (no auth) and type-2-only (DES challenge). Solid T1 for no-auth (server *declares* it will accept). Biggest gap: never actually accepts the security type - stops at 'server offered X'; a T2/T3 would send SecurityResult=OK and grab a framebuffer JPEG as proof-of-desktop. Also no support for capturing the DES challenge for offline hashcat -m 11600, and no default-password sweep against 'password'/'admin'/'12345678'/blank on type-2-only endpoints.

findings.tier_evidence: Server-sent security-type list includes 1 (None). Deterministic, single roundtrip, no auth attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Accept security type 1 (send byte 0x01, expect SecurityResult=0), then send ClientInit (byte 1 shared), read ServerInit (framebuffer W/H/pixelformat/name), send a FramebufferUpdateRequest, and screenshot the first raw-encoding rectangle to a PNG. That's genuine T3 initial-access - eyes on the console. Cap the capture at one small tile (128x128) to keep it lightweight.
findings.tester_next_step: vncviewer <ip>::<port>   # opens KVM immediately; capture with vncsnapshot <ip>::<port> screenshot.png   or scrot the vncviewer window.

findings.title_pattern: VNC offers only DES-based VNC Authentication (weak)
findings.tier_evidence: Security-type list == [2] - server itself declared VNC-Auth-only.
findings.promotion_notes: Send byte 0x02 to accept type 2, read the 16-byte challenge, and dump it as a hashcat -m 11600 candidate. Add a small dictionary check against ('password','admin','vnc','12345678','') as a T3 credential burn.

findings.tier_evidence: Version and security-type list only - straight banner.
findings.promotion_notes: Correct as info - all T1 claims fork off separate finding kinds.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -p <port> --script vnc-info,realvnc-auth-bypass <ip>   # covers RealVNC CVE-2006-2369 auth-bypass among others.
